screen.fiximizer.performance_intro: Choose Fiximizer's behavior. Profiles tune only Fiximizer-managed background work; they do not reprioritize Minecraft or other mods' internal threads.
screen.fiximizer.memory_guard_help: Automatic switch when heap stays above %s%%. Return after usage remains below %s%% for several samples.
screen.fiximizer.integrations_intro: Fiximizer checks the loaded ModContainer and version for each target. An integration stays gated when its mod is absent or its toggle is off. This release provides detection and guarded extension points; specific Create/Sable patches are still under development.
screen.fiximizer.integrations_detection_: Mod detection is disabled in settings.
screen.fiximizer.jvm_intro: The recommendation uses physical RAM and the loaded mod count. It only sets Xms/Xmx; Java 21's default garbage collector is left unchanged.
screen.fiximizer.jvm_restart_note: To apply these arguments, paste the first line into Prism Launcher → Edit Instance → Java → JVM arguments, then restart the game. A running JVM cannot change Xms/Xmx.

screen.fiximizer.physics_intro: Passive timings from recent physics steps. Sable is measured between its pre and post events: Java preparation, native physics, and pose updates are included, not just Rapier.

screen.fiximizer.frames_intro: Measures wall-clock time inside GameRenderer.render() and the client tick. It is not the actual interval between displayed frames and does not measure GPU execution.

screen.fiximizer.server_intro: Measures the full server tick between ServerTickEvent.Pre and Post. Available in a local single-player world.

screen.fiximizer.server_budget: The 20 TPS budget is 50 ms per tick. These timings include Create, Sable and all other server work; do not add them to the sub-profiler timings.

screen.fiximizer.startup_intro: Measures JVM-to-title-screen time and Fiximizer-owned startup phases. Optional mod detection and diagnostics start after 40 stable title/world ticks. Required NeoForge callbacks and other mods' lifecycle work are never skipped or reordered.

screen.fiximizer.memory.title: Memory optimizer
screen.fiximizer.memory.intro: Bounded, opt-in sharing of explicitly submitted immutable metadata. The cache is created only after first use; no heap scan, global object rewrite or recurring task is performed.
screen.fiximizer.memory.scope: Only explicitly submitted immutable strings are considered. A hit reuses a different equal String instance; zero hits means no savings were observed.
screen.fiximizer.memory.g1_note: G1 String Deduplication is optional and may add GC CPU work.
screen.fiximizer.memory.stats_hits: String reuse: %s duplicate hits from %s registrations
screen.fiximizer.memory.stats_evictions: Stale slots reused: %s | collision evictions: %s | contention bypasses: %s

screen.fiximizer.memory.compatible_fallb: No additional compact-header feature is exposed. Fiximizer keeps its compatible Java 21-targeted path.
screen.fiximizer.network_intro: Passive client-side observation of raw Netty traffic and server-reported ping. Auto compares Java and Rust for Fiximizer's local statistics workload. It does not replace Minecraft TCP with UDP or alter the server protocol.
screen.fiximizer.network_ping: Server-reported ping: %s ms | p50: %s ms | p95: %s ms | avg sample-to-sample ping change: %s ms
screen.fiximizer.network_backend: Statistics engine: %s | %s | Java %s ms | Rust %s ms
screen.fiximizer.network_native_times: Batch benchmark: Java %s ms | Rust %s ms
config.fiximizer.network.native_backend: Allow optional Rust native statistics backend
config.fiximizer.network.backend_mode: Network statistics backend mode (0 Auto, 1 Java, 2 Rust)
config.fiximizer.network.tcp_nodelay: Prefer TCP_NODELAY when supported and not managed by another stack optimizer
screen.fiximizer.gpu_intro: GPU telemetry and OpenCL capability checks. The benchmark is manual, bounded, and validates the GPU result against a CPU reference.
screen.fiximizer.gpu_test_result: Upload: %s ms | kernel: %s ms | download: %s ms
screen.fiximizer.gpu_test_total: GPU end-to-end: %s ms | CPU: %s ms | speedup: %s×
screen.fiximizer.vram_spill: Managed cache pool: %s budget | %s stored | %s blocks
screen.fiximizer.vram_spill_note: Only explicitly managed disposable cache data can use this pool. World and gameplay state are never stored there.
screen.fiximizer.simd_intro: A manual, isolated FMA-heavy compute test using the optional Rust library. It compares a portable scalar path with runtime-dispatched AVX2/FMA. This is a microbenchmark, not an FPS test; Minecraft world data is never touched.
